newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds remain dull despite limit-up Chicag.
newsitem.headline: European feeds remain dull despite limit-up Chicag.

text.p: The European meals and feeds market remained dull this afternoon despite a predicted limit-up Chicago soycomplex futures on the back of hot and dry weather in the U.S. midwest, market sources said.
Only one trade was reported at $260.50 a tonne fob Rotterdam for afloat material.

"This morning sellers upped their prices by as much as $9 in anticipation Chicago futures would open sharply up on hot and dry weather in the U.S. midwest. But buyers remained sidelined due to a higher dollar, which reached a six-year high," one broker said.
Dealers in Europe said buyers here usually are wary of taking positions in the first stages of a weather market.

"A weather market has its own way of trading. It has to be clear the weather did some damage to crops before European buyers enter the market and even then they act very carefully, unlike trading in Chicago where they buy the rumour and sell the fact," one dealer said.--KAREL LUIMES +31 20 504 5832
